newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kingsgate sees better 1997 revenue, profit. [CORRECTED 04:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Kingsgate sees better 1997 revenue, profit. [CORRECTED 04:45 GMT]

text.p: The chairman of New Zealand's Kingsgate International Limited hotels group Bruce Davidson said on Tuesday he expected improved net profit in the current year, driven by a growing income stream.
"The company now has two strong assets providing growing income streams. We expect enhanced revenues and net profitability in this year," he said in an address to the company's annual meeting.

Davidson said the company expected further improvement in the years to come as the Millennium Sydney reaped the benefits of the 2000 Olympic Games and as it realised development profits from Birkenhead Quays, alongside the enhancement of value of the Birkenhead Point shopping centre and marina complex in Sydney (corrects from Auckland to Sydney).
In calendar 1996 Kingsgate made a net proifit of NZ$2.56 million.
It is controlled by CDL Hotels New Zealand Limited, which is ultimately controlled by Singapore's Hong Leong Group via its investment arm CDL Hotels International.
